reason: Both reached the correct, honest conclusion (element most likely, board/wiring possible, engineer to test) without ordering a part prematurely. Conversation 1 was more useful: it explained why 'display shows level but no glow' points to the power side, gave the relay-click listening check, asked for and explained how to find the full model/PNC, and told the owner they can safely keep using the other zones. Conversation 2 was safe and correct but thinner, spent a turn on an induction/test-pan detour after the owner had already described the symptom, and never asked for the full model number. Conversation 1 loses a little for the odd 'software called hob' opener and for describing multimeter testing a homeowner who won't remove the hob can't do, though it hedged this with breaker isolation and a clear 'most people get an engineer' steer.
